code_review_findings: web_search.py clean_markdown() correctly strips '*', '**', headings '#', and backticks — regex looks solid.
_fix_marker_positions() shifts leading [n] markers to end of previous line via idempotent regex loop — correct.

ai_search uses 3 sequential calls (1 main + 2 supplementary) and dedupes by resolved final URL, flagging cited=true for in-text sources and cited=false for supplementary. UI consumes this correctly in App.js L591-595 (filter by cited, with ai-related-sources-label).
web_search prompts now ask for 'minimal 15 sumber' and run 3 calls (main + regulation-focused + news/analysis-focused). Merging/dedup logic uses priority sort — looks correct.
Cache TTL 600s with key=(kind, query.lower()) — pagination hits same cache key, so page=2 is served from memory. Verified.
renderAiAnswer in App.js L185-198 strips remaining '*' and leading '#' client-side as a double-safety net — good.
Potential issue: when all three LLM calls fail (e.g., budget error), ai_search raises, endpoint returns 502. Error surface could be more descriptive (budget vs other failures).
Minor: _grounded_call retries only on 'concurrent' or '429' + no 'budget' substring, which correctly bypasses retry on budget errors — good.

rca of the issue: RCA: 502 from /api/ai-search and /api/search is caused by EMERGENT_LLM_KEY exceeding its budget. Backend err log: 'litellm.RateLimitError: Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 1.0000466, Max budget: 1.0'. web_search._sequential_calls propagates this exception on the mandatory first call → endpoint catches generic Exception and raises HTTPException(502). Reproduction: POST /api/ai-search {q:'anything new'} — returns 502 in ~1.5s. Mitigation: top up or rotate the EMERGENT_LLM_KEY. Code mitigation: special-case 'budget' in error message to return a dedicated 503 with user-friendly detail.
